In one pathway, Acetylleucine directly targets Pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 component subunit alpha, testis-specific form, mitochondrial, which is then targeted by a compound with a known mode of action. This compound, [(3S,8R,10R)-8-hydroxy-3-methyl-5-oxo-2,9-dioxatricyclo[4.3.1.03,8]decan-10-yl]methyl benzoate, is known to inhibit Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. In the second pathway, Acetylleucine targets Guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2, which is targeted by n-acetyl serotonin, a compound that also interacts with Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The integration of these two pathways suggests that Acetylleucine may influence Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1 through different mechanisms, potentially involving enzyme inhibition or receptor modulation. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Acetylleucine and Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
